To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have introduced a new algorithm that allows for the interactive exploration of animated volume datasets; 2) the compression ratio can be optimized for visual artifacts or for the compression ratio; 3) the compression ratio is further enhanced by motion compensation techniques; 4) the resulting wavelet data is visualized in a high quality way using a number of novel visualization algorithms.

(1) the compression ratio of the wavelet coefficients is not affected by the order of the wavelet, (2) the compression ratio is not significantly affected by the family of wavelets used and (3) a motion compensation scheme can be applied without significantly degrading the visual quality of the reconstructed volume data.
we are capable of compressing a volume of size 256^3 at 24 bit color depth with a compression ratio of 20:1 and decompressing it in realtime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the compression of animated volume data, the decompression of this data in real-time and the display of these data in real-time.
real-time visualization of animated volume datasets.
a new method of real-time visualization of animated volume datasets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is capable to decompress and visualize an animation at interactive frame rate on a single PC.
we are able to decompress and visualize animated volume data at interactive frame rates with a high compression ratio and a high image quality.
the proposed method can be applied to any kind of wavelet and any kind of encoding scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to compress animated volume data at interactive frame rates with very high compression ratios, and to display the decompressed volumes at the same frame rate with high visual impression.
we are able to decompress and visualize a 3D volume animation of 512^3 voxels at interactive frame rates with a compression ratio of 10:1.
we are capable of compressing animated data sets of up to 1GB in size to about 5% of their original size and decompressing them in real time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interactive decompression and visualization is possible even for large datasets and that wavelet compression is a very suitable technique for interactive visualization.
the compression of animated volume data can be done at a high quality, with a high compression ratio, and at a high speed.
we can decompress and display a sequence of volume data at interactive rates on a standard workstation.
